sources.title: Greg W. Forbes, Leaving the Past Behind: A Sermon on 1 Peter 4:1–6
sources.claimLimit: Inspected sections support Forbes's own readings of 4:1 ceased-from-sin, 4:6 now-dead believers, 4:7–11 ethics, Prov 10:12 as possible background, and non-exhaustive gift examples. This is one evangelical witness, not consensus.

sources.title: Daniel C. Arichea and Eugene A. Nida, A Handbook on The First Letter from Peter (UBS, 1980), public passage excerpts
sources.claimLimit: Use only inspected passage-level commentary reproduced with permission. It maps translation/exegetical options, including 4:6 and 4:8; it is not open-license wholesale text and is not consensus.

sources.title: Sam Storms, 1 Peter Commentary, The Gospel Coalition Bible Commentary
sources.claimLimit: Relevant 4–5 sections were inspected. Supports Storms's stated interpretations, not neutral lexical facts or consensus. Particularly useful for 4:6, 5:1, 5:6–7, 5:12–13.

sources.title: Rahlfs-Hanhart LXX, Proverbs 10:12, Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft
sources.claimLimit: Supports exact LXX wording at Prov 10:12 for comparison with 1 Pet 4:8. Does not by itself prove Peter's transmission channel or authorial motive.

sources.title: Rahlfs-Hanhart LXX, Proverbs 11:31, Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft
sources.claimLimit: Supports exact LXX wording at Prov 11:31 for direct comparison with 1 Pet 4:18. Does not supply textual-critical witness distribution for 1 Peter.

sources.title: Rahlfs-Hanhart LXX, Proverbs 3:34, Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft
sources.claimLimit: Supports exact LXX wording at Prov 3:34 and the κύριος vs ὁ θεός comparison with 1 Pet 5:5. No authorial-motive claim.

sources.title: Jordan Atkinson, The Semantics of ἐν ᾧ in 1 Peter, The Bible Translator 72.1 (2021), 117–132
sources.claimLimit: Only abstract-level functional conclusions are used: causal 1:6/3:16/4:4; causal-concessive 2:12; dative-of-reference 3:19. Detailed argument is not claimed inspected.

sources.title: John H. Elliott, Elders as leaders in 1 Peter and the early Church, HTS 64.2 (2008)
sources.claimLimit: Abstract supports the elder/oversight/shepherd/flock cluster and its early-leadership significance. Detailed article claims require exact-body inspection before attribution.

sources.title: Gert Breed, The diakonia of the elder according to 1 Peter, In die Skriflig 50.3 (2016)
sources.claimLimit: Abstract supports Breed's explicit connection of 4:7–11 with 5:1–4 and diakonia framing. Do not turn one study into polity consensus.

sources.title: E. Randolph Richards, Silvanus Was Not Peter's Secretary, JETS 43.3 (2000), 417–432
sources.claimLimit: Supports attribution of Richards's thesis that γράφω διά + person points to a letter carrier rather than secretary. Full article argument was not inspected end-to-end here.

sources.title: NET Bible note on 1 Peter 5:12
sources.claimLimit: Supports NET's stated carrier-vs-amanuensis options and its preference for carrier. This is a translation-note judgment, not neutral consensus.

sources.title: Hugo A. Cotro, Historia de dos ciudades: Roma y Babilonia en el Apocalipsis, DavarLogos 21.2 (2022)
sources.claimLimit: Relevant section supports Cotro's circularity objection to proving Babylon=Rome by mutually appealing to 1 Peter and Revelation, and his rhetorical/exile alternative. It does not prove literal Mesopotamian Babylon or overturn consensus by itself.

sources.title: Roy Schroeder, The Babylon of 1 Peter 5:13, Concordia Seminary B.Div thesis (1954)
sources.claimLimit: Useful only as a history-of-interpretation map of Rome, Mesopotamian Babylon, and Egyptian Babylon theories; not a current scholarly arbiter.

sources.title: Dennis E. Johnson, Fire in God's House: Imagery from Malachi 3 in Peter's Theology of Suffering (1 Pet 4:12–19), JETS 29.3 (1986), 285–294
sources.claimLimit: Opening argument confirms Johnson's methodological claim that distant OT contexts/allusions matter and the article's Malachi-3 thesis. Full detailed Malachi argument remains HOLD because the rest of the body is subscription-gated.

sources.title: Christopher Byrley, Persecution and the 'Adversary' of 1 Peter 5:8, SBJT 21.3 (2017), 77–98
sources.claimLimit: Full Southern Equip web article was inspected. It supports Byrley's own survey of persecution models, warning against tying 1 Peter to one empire-wide official persecution solely from 4:16/5:9, and his cosmic-conflict reading of 5:8. One evangelical article is not consensus.

sources.title: Tyler Hallstrom, Like A Lion: Mapping the Leonine Metaphor in 1 Peter 5:8, JETS 65.3 (2022), 535ff.
sources.claimLimit: Abstract/opening only. Supports Hallstrom's comparison and synthesis of Jewish and Greco-Roman backgrounds and his warning against highly particularized one-background readings. Detailed article argument remains subscription HOLD.

sources.title: Jennifer Strawbridge, Spiders Are Bad Kissers: The Kiss of Love and the Holy Kiss in Early Christian Writings, Anglican Theological Review 107.4 (2025), 332–348
sources.claimLimit: Relevant 1 Peter 4:9 and 5:14 sections were inspected through publisher/indexed text; Oxford's official record verifies the article and CC BY 4.0 rights. Supports love/kinship/solidarity/hospitality and kiss-as-embodied-reconciliation themes, not a complete reconstruction of one local congregation's lodging system.

sources.title: NET Bible translation notes on 1 Peter 5:2–3
sources.claimLimit: Exact NET notes inspected. Supports the grammatical relation of participles to the shepherding command and the contextual gloss of τῶν κλήρων as those allotted/entrusted to the elders' care. It is not a critical apparatus substitute and not a full lexical history of κλῆρος.
